…Sedanka we were in possession of more than fifty ethnographical specimens. I had to hire an extra sledge to transport them to the big village of Tigil, which was our next destination, and where we were going to deposit our things, to be shipped afterwards for Petropavlovsk.

Following the course of the Sedanka and Tigil rivers, we came to the large village of Tigil, the most northern place we visited during the whole expedition. Here we added considerably to our ethnographical collections.

ROM Tigil we had a journey of about six | ee miles to Petropavlovsk. The greater part of it was over one continuous tundra. On this tundra lie eighteen Kamchadal villages situated at distances of from thirteen to fifty miles from each other. A great portion of the tundra is as level as the sea. You can see no end to it.
